# Larkspur Care Group — document library

The staff handbook is the binding reference for terms and conditions at all of
the group's residential homes and for the central support team. Each home also
keeps a local arrangements file written by its manager; those files record the
rota pattern for that home and do not change any entitlement set out in the
handbook.

People team: people.services@larkspurcare.example
Payroll queries: payroll@larkspurcare.example (five working days to answer)
files.handbook/staff-handbook.md:
# Staff handbook — Larkspur Care Group

Revision 9. In force from 1 October 2025. Issued by the people team and
reviewed each September.

## 1 Working hours

Full-time hours are 37.5 per week, worked to a rota agreed with the home
manager. Residents' routines come first, so shift patterns vary between homes.
Night work carries a premium of 12 per cent on the basic rate.

## 2 Probation

New starters complete a probation period of six months. The home manager meets
the employee at the end of the third month and again in the final week. A
probation period may be extended once, by no more than three months, where the
manager records the reasons in writing.

## 3 Annual leave

Annual leave is 33 days a year for a full-time employee, including the eight
public holidays observed in the group's published calendar. Leave is booked
through the home manager and carried over only with the manager's written
agreement.

## 4 Study leave

Employees may take up to 20 working days of paid study leave in any rolling
twelve-month period. Study leave covers attendance at a course, examination or
accredited training programme that is relevant to the employee's role and has
been agreed with the home manager beforehand. Requests reach the manager at
least four weeks before the first day of the course, and the home keeps a
record of the days taken. Unused study leave does not carry into the following
twelve-month period and is not paid in lieu.

## 5 Sickness and absence

Report sickness to the home before the start of the shift. The group pays
statutory sick pay from the fourth consecutive day of absence, and the group's
own scheme adds the balance of basic pay for the first three weeks of a
certified absence.

## 6 Uniform and laundry

The group provides tunics, aprons and non-slip footwear. Employees launder
their own uniforms unless the home runs an on-site laundry. Uniforms remain
the property of the group and are returned when employment ends.

## 7 Meals and rest breaks

A meal is provided without charge on any shift of six hours or more. Breaks
are taken away from the resident areas and are scheduled so that each unit
keeps its agreed staffing level at all times.
files.handbook/uniform-and-equipment-list.md:
# Uniform and equipment list — Larkspur Care Group

Issued alongside the handbook for home managers ordering supplies.

| Item | Supplied to | Replace when |
|---|---|---|
| Tunic, short sleeve | Care and nursing staff | Worn or faded |
| Tunic, long sleeve | Care staff on night duty | Worn or faded |
| Apron, disposable | All resident-facing staff | Every shift |
| Non-slip footwear | All resident-facing staff | Annually |
| Gloves, nitrile | All staff | Every task |
| Name badge | All staff | On a change of name |
| Moving-and-handling belt | Trained handlers | Every second year |
| Torch, hand | Night duty | On failure |

Ordering goes through the home manager; deliveries arrive on Tuesdays and
Thursdays. Specialist equipment for a named resident is ordered by the clinical
lead, not from this list.

turns.prompt: One of the home managers is planning rota cover and needs the study leave figure for the team. Under the Larkspur Care Group staff handbook, how many working days of paid study leave may an employee take in a rolling twelve-month period? Give the number on its own. Reply with only the final answer. If you cannot determine the answer, reply exactly UNKNOWN.
